question.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(-1)=\sqrt{3},\,{f}^{′}(-1)=\sqrt{3},\,g(-1)=-3,\,{g}^{′}(-1)=2
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=-1.$ Do not round the answer. 

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=-1}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=-1,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=-1} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(-1)g(-1)-f(-1){g}^{′}(-1)}{(g(-1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\cdot (-3)-\sqrt{3}\cdot (2)}{(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-3\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{3}}{9} \\  & =-\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
